<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par67" />{{GHGmargin-letter|67|h}}
'''6.''' The original vowel is retained, see f, (''a'') in the preformative of the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} {{GHGheb|text=יָסֹב}} for ''yă-sōb'' (cf. {{GHGpar|47|b|doublesign=1}}, {{GHGpar|63|b|nosign=1}}, and for verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} § 72); (''b'') in the {{GHGterm|perfect Niphʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=נָסַב}} for ''nă-săb'' ({{GHGpar|51|a}}); (''c'') in {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} {{GHGheb|text=הוּסַב}}, with irregular lengthening (no doubt on the analogy of verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״ו}}) for ''hōsăb'' from ''hŭ-sab'', imperfect {{GHGheb|text=יוּסַב}} from ''yŭ-sab'', &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|i}}
On the other hand, an already attenuated vowel (''i'') underlies the intransitive ''imperfects Qal'' with ''ă'' in the second syllable (probably for the sake of dissimilating the two vowels), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יֵמַר}} for ''yĭ-măr'' (see p); and in the preformative of {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הֵסֵב}} from ''hĭ-sēb'' (ground-form {{GHGheb|text=הַקְטֵל}}, {{GHGpar|53|a}}), as well as of the participle {{GHGheb|text=מֵסֵב}} (ground-form {{GHGheb|text=מַקְטֵל}}), on the analogy of the perfect. In the second syllable of the Perf. the underlying vowel is ''ĭ'', attenuated from an original ''ă'', which in the strong verb is abnormally lengthened to ''î'' ({{GHGpar|53|a}}). The ''ē'' lengthened from ''ĭ'' is, of course, only tone-long, and hence when without the tone and before {{GHGterm|Dageš forte}} we have e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הֲסִבּ֫וֹתָ}}. On the retention of the original ''ă'' in the second syllable, cf. v.

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|k}}
'''7.''' The ''tone'', as a general rule, tends to keep to the stem-syllable, and does not (as in the strong verb) pass to the afformatives {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=וּ}} and {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}} (2nd ''sing. fem. imperfect''); e.g. 3rd ''sing. fem. perfect'' {{GHGheb|text=חַ֫תָּה}}, in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=חָ֫תָּה}}; with {{GHGheb|text=ר}} and gutturals {{GHGheb|text=מָ֫רָה}} (for {{GHGheb|text=מַ֫רָּה}}), {{GHGheb|text=שָׁ֫חָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=44|verse=26}}; on the other hand, with {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}} {{GHGheb|text=וְרַבָּ֫ה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=6|verse=12}} (but {{GHGheb|text=וָחָֽיָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=1|verse=16}}). In the 3rd ''plur. perfect'' the tone-syllable varies; along with {{GHGheb|text=דַּ֫לּוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=קַ֫לּוּ}}, we also find {{GHGheb|text=דַּלּ֫וּ}} and {{GHGheb|text=קַלּ֫וּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=רַבּ֫וּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=59|verse=12}}, {{GHGheb|text=שַׁח֫וּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=3|verse=6}}, &c.; but in {{GHGterm|pause}} always {{GHGheb|text=חָ֫תּוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=תָּ֫מּוּ}}, &c. The tone likewise remains on the stem-syllable in the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} in {{GHGheb|text=תָּסֹ֫בִּי}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָסֹ֫בּוּ}}; {{GHGterm|perfect Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGheb|text=הֵסֵ֫בָּה}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֵסֵ֫בּוּ}}; {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=תָּסֵ֫בִּי}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָ֫סֵבּוּ}} &c. In the forms with separating vowels, the tone is moved forward to these vowels (or to the final syllable, cf. ee), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=סַבּ֫וֹתָ}}, {{GHGheb|text=תְּסֻבֶּ֫ינָה}}, &c.; except before the endings {{GHGheb|text=תֶם}} and {{GHGheb|text=תֶן}} in the {{GHGterm|perfect}}, which always bear the tone. This shifting of the tone naturally causes the shortening of the merely tone-long vowels ''ē'' and ''ō'' to ''ĭ'' and ''ŭ'' (or ''ŏ'', see n), hence {{GHGheb|text=הֲסִבּ֫וֹתָ}} from {{GHGheb|text=הֵסֵב}}, {{GHGheb|text=תְּסֻבֶּ֫ינָה}} from {{GHGheb|text=יָסֹב}}; on cases in which the vowel of the preformative becomes {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}, see above, f.

{{GHGmargin-letter|67|l}}
'''8.''' In several verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}, instead of {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, {{GHGterm|Puʿal}} and {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}}, the less frequent conjugation {{GHGterm|Pôʿēl}}, with its passive and reflexive, occurs (most probably on the analogy of the corresponding forms of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, cf. {{GHGpar|72|m}}), generally with the same meaning,<ref>Sometimes both {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} and {{GHGterm|Pôʿēl}} are formed from the same stem, though with a difference of meaning, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=רִצֵּץ|translate=to break in pieces}}, {{GHGheb|text=רֹצֵץ|translate=to oppress}}; {{GHGheb|text=חִנֵּן|translate=to make pleasing}}, {{GHGheb|text=חוֹנֵן|translate=to have pity}}; {{GHGheb|text=סִבֵּב|translate=to turn, to change}}, {{GHGheb|text=סוֹבֵב|translate=to go round, to encompass}}.</ref> e.g. {{GHGheb|text=עוֹלֵל|translate=to ill-treat}}, passive {{GHGheb|text=עוֹלַל}}, reflexive {{GHGheb|text=הִתְעוֹלֵל}} (from {{GHGheb|text=עָלַל}}; cf. the ''Hithpôʿēl'' from {{GHGheb|text=רָעַע}}<section end="par67" /><noinclude>
